e.meaning: tranquility, splendor; a name of the goddess Parvati
e.etymology: From Sanskrit Uma, a name of the Hindu goddess Parvati, wife of Shiva. As a word, uma can also mean 'tranquility', 'splendor', 'fame' or 'night'.

assoc.t: Uma Thurman, star of Pulp Fiction and Kill Bill
Uma, Ursula's daughter in Disney's Descendants

e.etymology: From Italian fiore, 'flower', with the diminutive ending -ella. It is also well used in Peru, Argentina and Uruguay.
A recent name used mostly by Spanish-speaking families, with the Y- opening of names like Yahir and Yeison. Its sound is close to Erik.
A respelling of Emerson, an English surname meaning 'son of Emery'. Emery is a Norman form of the Germanic name Emmerich.
A modern American coinage from the word brave with the -en ending of Draven and Haven. Its peak year, 2018, was also the year of Jason Momoa's action film Braven.

assoc.t: Braven, 2018 Jason Momoa action film

e.etymology: A respelling of Rosalie, the French form of Latin Rosalia, from rosa, 'rose', with the -leigh ending popular in 2010s America.
A respelling of Huntley, an English place name and surname from Old English hunta, 'hunter', plus leah, 'meadow, clearing'.
From the place name Astoria, coined in honor of fur magnate John Jacob Astor and borne by a city in Oregon and a neighborhood of Queens, New York.

assoc.t: Waldorf Astoria, the luxury hotel chain
Astoria, neighborhood in Queens, New York City
Astoria, Oregon, setting of The Goonies

e.etymology: A respelling of Hendrix, a Dutch and German surname meaning 'son of Hendrik', a form of Henry, 'home ruler'. Its use as a first name follows the fame of guitarist Jimi Hendrix.

assoc.t: Jimi Hendrix, the rock guitarist (spelled Hendrix)

e.etymology: A spelling of McKenna, from the Irish surname Mac Cionaoith, 'son of Cionaodh', an old Gaelic personal name also behind Kenneth.
Tennyson's form of the Welsh name Eluned, used in Idylls of the King and later read as Lynn plus -ette. Eluned comes from Welsh eilun, image or idol.
namesakes: Lynette Scavo (Felicity Huffman's character on Desperate Housewives)

e.etymology: From Spanish rocío, dew, shortened from María del Rocío, a title of the Virgin Mary honored at El Rocío in Almonte, Andalusia.
namesakes: Rocío Dúrcal (Spanish singer and actress beloved in Mexico)

e.etymology: A respelling of Liliana, also read as a blend of Lily and Anna. Liliana comes from Latin lilium, the lily.
A Spanish surname taken up as a first name by African American families after 1896 to honor Antonio Maceo, the Afro-Cuban general of Cuba's war for independence.
namesakes: Maceo Parker (funk saxophonist with James Brown)

e.etymology: A respelling of Malachi, from Hebrew mal'akhi, my messenger, the name of the last of the Old Testament's minor prophets.

assoc.t: Malachai, a cult enforcer in Children of the Corn

e.etymology: From Arabic bayan, clear expression or eloquence, a word used in the Quran. A separate Mongolian and Turkic men's name Bayan means rich.
A spelling of Eliana that follows the Hebrew, where the name reads as my God has answered. Eliana is also an Italian and Spanish name from the Roman family name Aelianus.

e.meaning: a crow-like bird; the castle piece in chess
e.etymology: The English word used as a name. The bird's name comes from Old English hroc, an imitation of its call; the chess rook comes through Old French from Persian rukh.

assoc.t: the castle piece in chess
rook, a European bird of the crow family
to rook someone is to cheat or swindle them
Rook, the Hasbro trick-taking card game

e.note: Rook is also an old verb meaning to swindle, and the name invites rookie jokes.

e.etymology: An English surname used as a first name. It is explained either as a nickname for a tall, thin person, from Middle English hoit, a long stick, or as a name for someone who lived on a hill.
namesakes: Hoyt Wilhelm (Hall of Fame knuckleball pitcher)

assoc.t: Hoyt, maker of archery bows

e.etymology: The Portuguese and Catalan form of Joanna, from Latin Joanna and Greek Ioanna, the feminine of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious.
An Italian form of Mirabel, from Latin mirabilis, wonderful or marvelous. Mirabella is also an Italian surname and place name.
A pet form of the Yiddish name Hersh, deer, the everyday partner of the Hebrew name Tzvi. It is used mainly in Hasidic communities, where pet forms are often the registered name.

assoc.t: Hershey's chocolate, spelled with an e but said the same

e.note: Sounds exactly like Hershey, the chocolate brand.

e.etymology: From Hebrew Eliav, built from El, God, and av, father. In the Bible Eliab is the eldest brother of King David, passed over when Samuel anoints the youngest.
From Arabic namir, leopard or tiger. In the United States it also sits with the family of names ending in -mir, such as Amir, Samir and Jamir.
A modern American name of unclear source, close in sound to Evan and Ian. It matches Evian, the bottled water named for the French spa town Évian-les-Bains.

assoc.t: Evian bottled water

e.note: Evian is a major bottled-water brand, and people like to point out that it spells naive backwards.

e.etymology: A spelling of Turkish Nazlı, from Persian naz, coyness or delicate charm, with the Turkish ending -lı, having. Queen Nazli of Egypt carried the name into Arabic use.
A Japanese name whose meaning depends on the characters chosen; one common writing combines small, night and village. It reached American parents through a video game character.

assoc.t: Sayori in the game Doki Doki Literature Club

e.note: Known in the US mainly from the horror game Doki Doki Literature Club, in which the character Sayori dies by suicide.

e.etymology: A pet form of Caroline used as an independent name since the 19th century. Caroline is a feminine form of Charles, from Germanic karl, free man.
namesakes: Carrie Fisher (Princess Leia in Star Wars)
Carrie Bradshaw (Sex and the City lead character)

assoc.t: Carrie, Stephen King's telekinetic prom-night outcast

e.etymology: A spelling variant of Holly, from the holly tree, Old English holegn. Holly came into use as a given name around 1900, often for girls born near Christmas.
A spelling variant of Erin, from Irish Éirinn, a form of Éire, the Irish name for Ireland. Erin became a given name outside Ireland in the 20th century.

e.meaning: from the Scottish island of Iona
e.etymology: From the Hebridean island of Iona, where St Columba founded his monastery in 563. The island's name probably arose from a misreading of Latin Ioua, from Old Irish Í, perhaps yew place.

assoc.t: Iona, the holy island in Scotland's Hebrides
Iona University in New York, home of the Gaels

e.note: Said aloud, Iona sounds like the phrase I own a, an old source of jokes.

e.etymology: From Old Norse Þórr, the hammer-wielding god of thunder, from Proto-Germanic *Þunraz, thunder. The same root gives English thunder and Thursday.
namesakes: Thor Heyerdahl (Norwegian explorer of the Kon-Tiki voyage)

assoc.t: Marvel's Thor, played by Chris Hemsworth
the Norse god of thunder
